title: Quantitation of methanol, ethyl acetate, and fusel oils in distilled spirits by gas chromatography
author: Owens, Lowe

steps.title: Prepare analyte stock solution
steps.instruction: In a 100 mL volumetric flask add the following amounts and fill to volume with Omni‑Pur ethanol: methanol 20.0 mL (≈20.0 mg mL⁻¹), ethyl acetate 2.00 g (20.0 mg mL⁻¹), n‑propanol 1.00 g (10.0 mg mL⁻¹), isobutanol 2.00 g (20.0 mg mL⁻¹), n‑butanol 1.00 g (1.00 mg mL⁻¹), active amyl alcohol 2.00 g (20.0 mg mL⁻¹), isoamyl alcohol 2.00 g (20.0 mg mL⁻¹). Mix thoroughly and bring to exactly 100 mL.

steps.title: Make six calibration standards
steps.instruction:
Using the stock solution, prepare six calibration levels in 25.0 mL volumetric flasks with ethanol/water (40/60, v/v) to obtain the concentrations shown in Table 2: 
- Ethyl acetate: 25, 50, 100, 200, 500, 1600 mg L⁻¹
- Methanol: 0.025, 0.050, 0.100, 0.200, 0.500, 1.600 % v/v
- n‑Propanol: 12.5, 25, 50, 100, 250, 800 mg L⁻¹
- Isobutanol: 25, 50, 100, 200, 500, 1600 mg L⁻¹
- n‑Butanol: 1.25, 2.50, 5.0, 10, 25, 80 mg L⁻¹
- Amyls (active + isoamyl): 50, 100, 200, 400, 1000, 3200 mg L⁻¹
Store the flasks at 8 °C. Before use, allow them to warm to 20 °C and pipette 1.00 mL of each standard into a 20 mL glass vial for headspace sampling.

steps.title: Prepare HS calibration vials
steps.instruction: For each calibration standard add 1.00 mL to a 20 mL glass vial, then add 4 mL deionized water containing 10 % w/v sodium chloride. Cap with a crimped septum‑lined aluminum cap, shake by hand for 30 s, and keep the vial on the autosampler tray at room temperature (≈20 °C) until injection.

steps.title: Generate HS calibration curves
steps.instruction: Inject the prepared HS vials on the headspace‑GC/FID system, record the peak area for each analyte, plot area (y‑axis) versus concentration (x‑axis), fit the data with 1/x weighting using ChemStation software, and calculate LOD (3 × S/N) and LOQ (10 × S/N). Using the n‑butanol Level 1 standard (1.25 mg L⁻¹) the LOD was 0.35 mg L⁻¹ and the LOQ 1.17 mg L⁻¹; these values are applied to all analytes.

steps.title: Analyze spirits by HS‑GC/FID
steps.instruction: For each distilled‑spirit sample (whiskey, bourbon, rum, tequila, cachaça, gin) pipette 1.00 mL into a 20 mL glass vial, add 4 mL water with 10 % w/v NaCl, cap, shake 30 s, let stand at 20 °C, then place on the autosampler for analysis under the same HS‑GC/FID conditions used for the standards.

steps.title: Spike‑recovery validation (HS)
steps.instruction: Select three spirits (rum, gin, cachaça) and spike each at two levels: Level A – methanol 0.050 % v/v, ethyl acetate 50 mg L⁻¹, n‑propanol 25 mg L⁻¹, isobutanol 50 mg L⁻¹, n‑butanol 2.5 mg L⁻¹, amyls 100 mg L⁻¹; Level B – methanol 0.025 % v/v, ethyl acetate 25 mg L⁻¹, n‑propanol 12.5 mg L⁻¹, isobutanol 25 mg L⁻¹, n‑butanol 1.25 mg L⁻¹, amyls 50 mg L⁻¹. Prepare spiked samples as in the HS‑GC/FID sample‑preparation step, analyze on three separate days within a ten‑day period, and calculate % recovery using %Recovery = 100 × (Conc_spiked − Conc_unspiked) / Amount_added. Report %RSD for each analyte.

steps.title: Prepare DI calibration vials
steps.instruction: Transfer 1.00 mL of each analytical standard into amber 2.0 mL autosampler vials equipped with PTFE‑lined septa and screw caps. Keep the vials at room temperature on the autosampler tray until injection.

steps.title: Run DI‑GC/FID analysis
steps.instruction: Inject 1.0 µL of each standard or spirit sample directly onto a Hewlett‑Packard 5890 GC/FID equipped with an Agilent DB‑624 megabore column (30 m × 0.530 mm, 3.0 µm film). Set injector temperature to 250 °C. Oven program: 40 °C initial hold 6.00 min, ramp at 10.0 °C min⁻¹ to 220 °C, hold 1.00 min (total run 27.0 min). Use nitrogen as carrier gas with column head pressure 3.6 psi; equilibrate column 0.10 min between injections. Generate calibration curves (area vs concentration) with 1/x weighting using ChemStation v A.10.02; LOD, LOQ and calibration ranges follow the US‑TTB method SSD:TM:200, rev 9.
